programs.name: Basketball Post-Season
programs.audience: For high school athletes finishing a basketball season.
programs.note: Active rest, not a lifting program. Three weeks to let the body and the schedule recover. Start the Basketball Off-Season program after this.

guidance: Take 3 weeks off structured basketball training. Play other sports or games for fun: soccer, volleyball, swimming, pickup games of anything.
Move every day in an easy way: walk, bike, swim or shoot around with friends. Keep it light enough to hold a conversation.
The two sessions below are optional, 1-2 times a week, at an easy effort (RPE 5). Skip them if you are playing another sport.
Sleep and eat well; this is when the season's wear settles down.
If an athlete is coming back from an injury, a clinician decides when to start and when to move on.
Start the Basketball Off-Season program after this, in the week after week 3.

programs.audience: For high school tennis players, singles and doubles.
programs.note: A 4-week maintenance block that repeats all season. Two short sessions a week. programs.name: Tennis Post-Season
programs.audience: For high school athletes finishing a tennis season.
programs.note: Active rest, not a lifting program. Three weeks to let the body and the schedule recover. Start the Tennis Off-Season program after this.

guidance: Take 3 weeks off structured tennis training. Play other sports or games for fun: basketball, soccer, swimming, cycling.
Move every day in an easy way: walk, bike, swim or shoot around with friends. Keep it light enough to hold a conversation.
The two sessions below are optional, 1-2 times a week, at an easy effort (RPE 5). Skip them if you are playing another sport.
Sleep and eat well; this is when the season's wear settles down.
If an athlete is coming back from an injury, a clinician decides when to start and when to move on.
Start the Tennis Off-Season program after this, in the week after week 3.

programs.name: Golf Off-Season
programs.audience: For high school golfers.
programs.note: Eight weeks in two 4-week blocks. Block 1 builds muscle and work capacity (moderate loads, 8-12 reps); block 2 builds basic strength (80-90% 1RM, 3-6 reps). Weeks 4 and 8 are lighter: drop one set from every exercise and use about 90% of that block's load. Golf loads the lower back, the lead hip and the wrists most, so every session ends with trunk endurance, hip rotation strength and wrist work. Med ball throws carry the power work; few jumps are needed.
